name: Bimax / double jaw surgery

lead: Bimax means operating on both jaws in one procedure, typically a Le Fort I osteotomy of the upper jaw and a bilateral sagittal split osteotomy of the lower jaw. It changes the profile, bite and jawline and is used for dentofacial deformities, jaw asymmetry, airway obstruction and facial disproportion.

The jaw bones are cut and moved into new positions, then held with plates and screws while they heal. The facial change is visible after swelling settles. Looksmaxxing communities treat it as a major hardmaxx option for changing facial structure.

paras: Surgeons combine it with orthodontic treatment (braces) before and after the operation. Recovery involves weeks of restrictions, a liquid diet for a time, and months for full bone healing.

Reported risks include bleeding, swelling, infection (up to 7% reported) and facial numbness from nerve injury, which usually recovers within about three months but is rarely permanent. Surgery is performed by oral and maxillofacial or plastic surgeons.

angle.text: Bimax surgery is the forum term for orthognathic surgery that moves both jaws, sought for a more defined profile and corrected bite. The jaw bones are cut and repositioned, and the facial change is visible after healing. The procedure has documented functional benefits.

lead: Bimaxillary or 'bimax' surgery is orthognathic surgery in which both jaws are repositioned together, commonly a Le Fort I osteotomy of the maxilla combined with a bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) of the mandible [1]. Wikipedia lists it among the main orthognathic procedures alongside genioplasty [1].

It is used to correct dentofacial deformities, malocclusion, jaw asymmetry and obstructive sleep apnea, usually after orthodontic preparation [1]. In looksmaxxing culture the term is shorthand for the most comprehensive form of jaw surgery.
infobox: Le Fort I, BSSO, sometimes genioplasty
Initial healing 2 to 6 weeks; bone healing a further 2 to 4 months (per Wikipedia)
Oral and maxillofacial or plastic surgeon with orthodontist

paras: The Le Fort I cuts and repositions the upper jaw, and the BSSO, developed by Hugo Obwegeser, splits the lower jaw on each side so it can be moved. Both are fixed with plates and screws, and a chin procedure may be added [1].

Wikipedia reports that orthognathic surgery treats obstructive sleep apnea with high success rates and can improve facial aesthetics and self-esteem [1]. Surgery is typically preceded by orthodontic treatment lasting up to about a year [1]. A fuller review of orthognathic outcomes is given in the wiki's Jaw surgery / orthognathic entry.
No studies found specific to the looksmaxxing label 'bimax' in the sources reviewed for this entry.

According to Wikipedia, complications include bleeding, swelling, infection (up to 7% in cited figures) and numbness from inferior alveolar nerve injury, which usually recovers within three months [1]. Initial recovery takes 2 to 6 weeks and weight loss is common [1].
